evidence.text: The entry gives competing analyses of early forms: some oracle-bone forms are analyzed as 步 with 戉 as phonetic, while another account says 戉 was borrowed to write 歲 and later graphically distinguished. It reports oracle-bone use for ‘year’ and bronze examples for ‘year/years’, but does not establish a single origin or continuous semantic sequence. For small seal script, it reports 从步、戌聲. Its account explains the year sense through Jupiter’s circuit; that is the database’s interpretation.

gaps: The oracle-bone and bronze examples are reported by CUHK, but primary inscriptions and their full contexts were not inspected here; the earliest sense and precise dates remain unresolved.

Early graphic accounts conflict: CUHK reports both a 步-plus-戉 analysis and borrowing/differentiation from 戉. The transmitted seal analysis 步 plus 戌 is a later lexicographic account, not proof of the graph’s original formation.

The depicted weapon’s ancient spoken name is not established in the inspected sources. A proposed phonetic role for 戉 therefore does not by itself demonstrate a weapon-name-to-year-word sound borrowing.
No verified source here establishes a continuous semantic chronology among ritual use, year/harvest, age, and Jupiter. The Jupiter-to-year explanation is a reported calendrical interpretation.

The local packet’s Mandarin and Baxter–Sagart rows are not external evidence. Official per-character Unihan pages and the Baxter–Sagart primary table were not successfully inspected in this invocation, so no paired historical pronunciation claim is added.
The cited simplified-form lineage from cursive 歲 to 岁 remains supported only by dossier material in this task; it was not independently reverified in this web pass.

Bulk reuse of CUHK material is not recommended: its reuse terms for repeated database extracts were not verified. The selected Commons glyph is a single public-domain modern redraw, not evidence for an ancient artifact image.
